query: For refractory high-entropy alloys intended as energetic structural materials, what single testable hypothesis identifies an intervention that could improve ductility and uniform deformability without sacrificing high strength or impact-induced energy release? State the proposed intervention, its hypothesized mechanism, the improvement expected relative to the untreated baseline, the conditions under which it should hold, the prior evidence supporting it, and a decisive experiment that could falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a controlled, low level of interstitial oxygen doping into refractory high-entropy alloys (such as fine-grained CoCrNiV) will modestly raise the stacking fault energy so as to promote uniform dislocation glide rather than twinning, thereby enhancing ductility and uniform deformability without compromising the high strength or impact-induced energy release of the alloy.
generation.material_initial_state: A refractory high-entropy alloy (e.g., CoCrNiV) with a single-phase, fine-grained FCC microstructure exhibiting high yield strength (~1060 MPa) and moderate uniform elongation (~24%).
generation.intervention: Controlled interstitial oxygen doping at a low concentration that does not destabilize the FCC single-phase structure.
generation.conditions: Under room temperature quasi-static tensile and impact loading conditions, with the alloy retaining its fine-grained morphology after standard rolling and heat treatment.
generation.structural_mediator: A modest elevation in the stacking fault energy mediated by interstitial oxygen atoms.
generation.mechanism: Oxygen atoms occupy interstitial sites and increase the stacking fault energy, which suppresses deformation twinning and encourages a deformation mode dominated by uniform dislocation glide. This mechanism should improve ductility while preserving the alloy’s strength and its capacity for energy release under impact.
generation.predicted_outcome: An increase in uniform elongation and improved strain-hardening behavior (enhanced ductility) without a statistically significant reduction in yield strength or impact energy absorption compared to the untreated alloy.
generation.baseline: Untreated refractory HEA with a fine-grained FCC structure showing ~1060 MPa yield strength and ~24% uniform elongation.
generation.boundary: This effect is expected only for modest oxygen doping levels that maintain the alloy's single-phase FCC structure and fine-grained morphology; higher doping levels or process deviations could lead to unwanted phase transformations or degradation of mechanical properties.
generation.uncertainty: The precise magnitude of improvement in ductility and the optimal oxygen concentration remain uncertain and will require systematic experimental calibration.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of refractory HEA samples (e.g., CoCrNiV) using identical processing (rolling and heat treatment), one set doped with a controlled, low concentration of oxygen and the other as an untreated control. Subject both sets to room temperature tensile and impact tests and perform in-situ transmission electron microscopy (TEM) to observe deformation mechanisms.
measurements: Stacking fault density and dislocation activity via TEM
Phase stability and microstructural consistency via XRD and SEM
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the oxygen-doped samples do not exhibit a statistically significant improvement in uniform elongation and strain-hardening behavior compared to the control while maintaining similar yield strength and impact energy absorption, or if doping induces unwanted phase transformations (e.g., formation of brittle intermetallics or excessive twinning), the hypothesis will be falsified.

Fully recrystallized FG Co33Cr24Ni33V10 alloys, CR750 and CR800, were produced by cold rolling at room temperature and heat treatment. By conducting tensile tests and microstructure characterization, the main conclusions can be summarized as follows: The Co33Cr24Ni33V10 alloy maintained a single-phase FCC structure and exhibited superior phase stability throughout the processes of rolling, heat treatment, and tensile deformation. The primary deformation mechanisms of the CR750 and CR800 alloys were dislocation slip and SFs, with no occurrence of twinning or phase transformation. The fully recrystallized FG structure of CR750 alloy with the minimum mean grain size of 0.95 μm exhibited a high yield strength of 1060 MPa and a uniform elongation of 24.1%. The exceptional strength can be attributed to the presence of the FG structure and solid solution strengthening effect, while the remarkable ductility arises from the excellent strain-hardening ability primarily governed by dislocations and SFs.

This study employed first-principles calculations combined with the Special Quasi-random Structure (SQS) technique to systematically investigate the effects of interstitial elements C, N, and O on the structural, electronic, and mechanical properties of NiCoCr medium-entropy alloys (MEAs). The key findings are summarized as follows: Interstitial site preference and lattice distortion: C and N preferentially occupy octahedral interstitial sites, while O exhibits a higher diffusion rate between octahedral and tetrahedral sites, effectively alleviating stress concentration. The dissolution of these interstitial atoms causes significant lattice distortion, with O causing the most noticeable distortion (16.82%), followed by N (10.84%) and C (9.27%). Mechanical properties: The introduction of interstitial atoms increases the elastic constants and SFE, indicating an improvement in stiffness and resistance to plastic deformation. O doping leads to the most significant increase in SFE (69 mJ/m2, from −35 mJ/m2 to 34 mJ/m2), followed by N (58 mJ/m2) and C (54 mJ/m2). reading.lever: Controlled interstitial oxygen doping to modestly raise stacking fault energy, thereby promoting uniform dislocation glide.
reading.why: Prior simulation and experimental studies in NiCoCr and metastable HEAs indicate that minor oxygen interstitials can improve ductility without compromising strength or impact energy release.
